scope: One exact-head Android 4.1 window comparing the automatic ordinary compiled-program owner with the experimental structural Element Template owner for a native-tap 1,000-row create. This is a configuration-level same-device comparison, not a general Android, iOS, memory, list, no-JIT, cross-framework, or default-switch claim.

candidate.ordinaryConfiguration: production automatic core with the ordinary compiled-program native owner
candidate.structuralElementTemplateConfiguration: production automatic core with compiler-proved structural Element Template ownership

protocol.mainBoundary: compact product receiver frame application through ACK and complete dispatch
protocol.devtool: disabled by a background-only preflight before every sample; no CDP connection used
protocol.input: native ADB tap at the registered create-1,000 control

instrumentedBundles.interpretation: The differing app-bundle engine versions are inherent to the two current encoder configurations, so latency is attributed to the complete configurations rather than to one primitive in isolation.

frameBytes.interpretation: The payload is effectively unchanged and does not explain the latency win.

sourceReport.sanitization: The compact record excludes the raw device endpoint, local paths, timestamps per event, raw log lines, and generated row labels.

decision.comparativeConfigurationResult: structural Element Template was faster in all 10 pairs at both registered latency boundaries
remaining: fresh-process peak/settled/after-clear native memory and GC cycles
